raw: {"triples": [{"subject": "Experiments", "predicate": "uses", "object": "10 established probing task datasets", "object_type": "Dataset", "source_sentence": "In our experiments we use 10 established probing task datasets for the English language introduced by Conneau et al."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "sub-word tokens", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "While BERT uses sub-word tokens to get around out of vocabulary tokens, in the rare instance of encountering an OOV with GloVe, we generate a random word embedding in its stead."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT model", "predicate": "uses", "object": "pytorch_pretrained_bert library", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "we used the bert-base-uncased BERT model from the pytorch_pretrained_bert library"}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "scikit-learn MLP implementation", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "for the MLP probe we used the scikit-learn MLP implementation using the default parameters"}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "sentence embeddings", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Finally, we use the vanilla BERT and GloVe sentence embeddings in their respective evaluations as vanilla baselines against which the models with noise are compared."}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "sentence embeddings", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Finally, we use the vanilla BERT and GloVe sentence embeddings in their respective evaluations as vanilla baselines against which the models with noise are compared."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "GloVe Vectors", "predicate": "comparesAgainst", "object": "random baselines", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "The vanilla GloVe vectors out- perform the random baselines on all tasks except BS."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "specifically BERT stores information pertinent to the BS, SOMO and TC tasks in the norm."}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "while GloVe uses it to store SL, WC, TC and TD information."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "vector norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Given that we know that BERT is a contextual encoder, and that its self-attention uses the vector norm to control the levels of contribution from less informative words , we suspect that this gives it the capabilities to accurately model these short-distance dependencies and word co-occurrence probabilities, concepts which strongly correspond to local contextual incongruity."}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "In contrast, GloVe is a static encoder and exhibits no indication that it stores this information in the norm, or indeed any ability to accurately model this phenomenon at all, but uses the norm to store surface-level and syntactic information."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "GloVe uses the norm to encode sentence length, as reflected in our experiments in §4."}]}

{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Our findings show that BERT primarily uses the norm to store contextual incongruity information and positions incongruous sentences closer to the origin."}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Other", "source_sentence": "Meanwhile, GloVe stores much more syntactic information in its norm than BERT, but does not store contextual information at all, and mainly stores surface-level information in the norm."}]}
